ashley.t: heads-up from an int8 onboarding sweep for orion-lite -> gemma-compat: we see a reproducible top-token flip for summaries when rotary_scale != 1.0. looks like rotary scaling interplay with token ids after nfkc normalization.

ben.p: do we see same on fp16 or fp32? could be quant noise.

ashley.t: fp16 baseline is stable. int8 shift happens across multiple seeds and only when tokenizer run is set to normalize_nfkc=true. small repro below.

ashley.t: ```
# repro command
python -m rwinf.eval \n  --model orion-lite-gemma-int8 \n  --prompt tests/longctx/summaries/issue_set.txt \n  --rotary-scale 0.7 \n  --tokenizer-normalize nfkc \ 
  --topk 5
```

sophia.r: can you paste the token sequences (pre and post normalization) where the flip happens? might be a tokenizer mapping collision.

ashley.t: pasted in the ticket T12901. example: pre-nfkc token ids: [45, 1023, 17, 9, 2] -> post-nfkc: [45, 1023, 17, 9, 2] (same) but after conversion to gemma layout token id 9 maps to a different embed slot because of our vocab remap script that dedupes compat tokens.

ben.p: ah: we recently changed remap to collapse invisible-control tokens into lower ids to save embedding slots. that remap combined U+200D variants which only appear after nfkc normalization. if that causes a token id shift the rotary sin/cos table index also shifts and with non-1.0 scale the attention pattern changes nonlinearly.

ashley.t: exactly. i tracked attention scores for head 3 layer 7: with scale=1.0 topk matches fp16; with scale=0.7 the key-query dot product magnitude shrinks and the slightly shifted embedding yields a different argmax. per-prompt delta in logit gap ~0.6 -> token flip in ~37% of cases on our 200-sample eval.

sophia.r: plan: 1) revert the remap for tokens that are only introduced by normalization; 2) add a mapping sanity check in conversion that compares embedding_index(token) before/after normalization and flags >0 shifts; 3) run rotary-scale sweep to find safe quantized scale. i'll take (1) and (2).

ben.p: also add a quick unit that runs small-attention sanity: pick small vocab subset, apply remap, compute rotary indices and assert they remain stable for tokens present in baseline.

ashley.t: created phab T12902 and attached a tiny repro archive (tests/eng-ml/orion_remap_repro.tar.gz). i also uploaded a short notebook showing the attention-score delta heatmap. link: https://internal/redwood/tmp/orion_remap_repro (restricted).

ci-bot: CI started for branch fix/orion-remap-guard (job 10112). :gear:

ben.p: quick note: the rotary_scale param is exposed in runtime config for backward compatibility; maybe we should document that non-1.0 values can amplify token mapping bugs. add one-liner to onboarding checklist.

ashley.t: PR up that reverts the aggressive remap for nfkc-only tokens and adds conversion-time assertion. https://internal/redwood/pull/4901 (w/ unit). local eval shows topk matches restored to 98% vs fp16 (was 63%).

ben.p: nice. once CI green run full 1k prompt sweep and also test with mistral-converted variants — same remap codepath used there.

sophia.r: on it. will sweep rotary_scale in [0.6,0.8,1.0,1.2] and log rouge/accuracy. posting results in T12902 when done.

ashley.t: thanks. adding a note to conversion README: "Do not collapse tokens introduced only by tokenizer normalizations; keep embedding indices stable to avoid rotary index shifts".

ben.p: resolved for now pending CI and the full sweep. leaving this thread for records. :eyes:
